findings.body:
**Include `usageSummary` in the exact refusal assertion.**

`makeReviewAddressMany` adds a `usageSummary` property to every result that does not have `status: 'ok'`. This test expects a non-`ok` refusal to equal `{ status, reason }` exactly, so the extra defined property makes `toEqual` fail. Add the property to the expected object so the assertion matches the public result shape.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   expect(result).toEqual({
     status: 'needs-human',
     reason: 'Prepared dependency root outside PR selection',
+    usageSummary: expect.any(Object),
   });
```

</details>
findings.title: Include `usageSummary` in the exact refusal assertion.

findings.body:
**Pass `managedSubmit` to this test. Without it, the CodeRabbit leg cannot launch a review, and the CLI-call assertion cannot hold.**

`makeReviewRun` is called without `managedSubmit` (lines 277-284). The CodeRabbit leg forwards `managedSubmit` only when it is defined (`src/ops/review/run.ts:382`). `dev.review` then returns `needs-human` when the CodeRabbit reviewer has no `managedSubmit`, and it does not fall back to the CLI (`src/ops/dev/review.ts:546-550`). The `coderabbit` command is never launched. The assertions at lines 291-295 expect one terminal CodeRabbit source and one `coderabbit` call, so they fail.

Inject the managed submit fixture as the sibling tests do. `settledPredecessorFindings.freshChangedHead.test.ts:42` passes `managedSubmit: managedTerminal([])`:

```diff
     const result = await makeReviewRun({
       drivers: cleanDrivers(),
       queueClient: terminal.client,
       effectsFactory: () => f.effects,
       noteLedgerWrite: note,
+      managedSubmit: managedTerminal([]),
       scannerFactory: () => async (components) =>
         components.map((component) => ({ component: component.component, hits: [] })),
     })({ repoRoot: f.repo.root });
```

Import or define `managedTerminal` in this file, using the same helper the sibling test uses. Change the CLI-call assertion at line 295 to expect zero `coderabbit` calls, as `freshChangedHead.test.ts:60` does. Check the other tests in this file that expect a terminal CodeRabbit result and that call `makeReviewRun` without `managedSubmit`. The prior review notes name the calls near lines 350-356 and 386-392. Those call sites were not inspected in this check.
findings.title: Pass `managedSubmit` to this test. Without it, the CodeRabbit leg cannot launch a review, and the CLI-call assertion cannot hold.

findings.body:
**The injected round-1 finding cannot fire, so round 2 never starts.**

The scripted reviewer returns its finding only when a prompt contains `-export const a = "BAD"` (test/ops/review/addressPinBase.test.ts:201-206). Re-review prompts compare the pinned base, `origin/main`, with the head. That base has no `src/a.ts`, so the comparison adds `+export const a = "BAD"` and never removes it. No re-review prompt contains the `-` line.

Without the finding, round 1 has no open findings after its re-review. The run finishes before round 2. The round-2 thread `T2`, the flip, and the `+export const a = "BEST"` assertion (about lines 311-316) are never reached, so the test cannot pass as written. Either the trigger must match a prompt that round 1 actually dispatches, or the re-review must use the seed commit as its base. The author must choose which. The comments and assertions must then describe the chosen comparison.
findings.title: The injected round-1 finding cannot fire, so round 2 never starts.
